shortDescription: West African crude oil differentials remained supported on Wednesday as disruption in the Middle East was expected to boost demand for alternative grades.

children: West African crude oil differentials remained supported on Wednesday as disruption in the Middle East was expected to boost demand for alternative grades.
Nigerian grade Qua Iboe was offered at dated Brent plus $6 and Bonga at dated plus $9, a trader said this week, adding that no deals had been concluded at those levels.
"The market is hot," a trader said.
In the wider market, Nigeria's Dangote oil refinery has issued a tender to sell up to 130,000 metric tons of residual fuel oil in late September, according to a document summary seen by Reuters.
